topic: Using an IpcValue proxy type instead of shoehorning unsupported types into serde for IPC boundaries
principle: When a type (e.g., Arc<dyn Array>) is fundamentally incompatible with serde's serialization model, do not attempt to derive or implement Serialize/Deserialize on it. Instead, define a lightweight proxy/enum type (e.g., IpcValue) that matches the IPC domain's data model and convert to/from the unsupported type at the boundary.
instruction: When building an IPC protocol that must pass types like Arc<dyn Array> (or any type with non-serializable ownership, trait object vtables, or internal pointers), create a dedicated proxy type that enumerates the supported data shapes. Serialize the proxy over the wire, then reconstruct the original type on the receiving side. This keeps serde traits implemented only on simple, owned enums and avoids fragile custom Serialize/Deserialize impls on complex types.
